name: systemd
description: Read-only systemd inspection for Claude on Linux — list units, get status, tail the journal, find failed services, and inspect unit files.
long_description:
Lets Claude answer the most common Linux ops question — _"why is this service broken?"_ — without you having to ssh in and run `systemctl status` yourself. Seven tools cover unit listing, per-unit status, journal tailing, failed-unit hunting, unit-property inspection, raw unit-file display (including drop-ins), and queued-job inspection.

**Strictly read-only in v0.1.** No restart, enable/disable, or daemon-reload. Safe on production hosts. If you want destructive control, run those commands manually via [claude-terminal-mcp](https://github.com/LukeLamb/claude-terminal-mcp) — keeping them out of this extension means it can be enabled on shared/sensitive systems without trust concerns.

**Both system and user scopes supported** via a `scope` arg defaulting to `system`. Set `scope: "user"` to inspect `--user` units (graphical sessions, per-user agents).

tools.name: list_units
tools.description: List systemd units with optional state and type filters. Returns unit name, load/active/sub state, and description per entry.

tools.name: failed_units
tools.description: Shortcut for the most common systemd query: list every unit currently in the failed state.

tools.name: unit_status
tools.description: Detailed per-unit status: active/sub state, enabled state, main PID, recent journal lines. The 'is this service healthy?' primitive.

tools.name: unit_show
tools.description: Full property dump from `systemctl show` (parsed Key=Value) for a single unit. Useful for inspecting Environment vars, ExecStart, Restart policy, drop-ins.

tools.name: unit_cat
tools.description: Raw text of a unit file plus all its drop-in overrides — exactly what `systemctl cat <unit>` prints. Use when you need to see what's actually loading.

tools.name: tail_journal
tools.description: Read recent journal entries with optional unit filter, priority filter, and time window. Returns parsed entries with timestamp, priority, and message.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: List queued/running systemd jobs (rare — useful when something is hanging during boot or a service is stuck activating).
